candidate_surface_pixel.surface: Visible PCB-up planar surface near the +x terminal region and toward its lower-y side; an upper-contact neighborhood, not a certified edge or contact patch.

closing_axis_world_if_justified.status: Conditional sideways thickness-pinch hypothesis. The observed plane justifies this normal direction, but no opposing contact is observed. Axis sign is interchangeable.

approach_direction_world_if_justified.status: Hypothesized inward reach from beyond the observed +x terminal boundary. This is an approach direction, not evidence of a clear approach corridor.

first_bounded_step.type: Simulator-only, no-contact reorientation proposal; not execution authorization.
first_bounded_step.orientation_goal: Make the jaw-closing axis parallel to the PCB normal and the finger insertion direction horizontal toward world -x. This requires turning the hand onto its side, not simply translating the current hand sideways.
first_bounded_step.jaw_action: Keep the current aperture unchanged; no closure.
first_bounded_step.bounds_and_gate: Propose only one orientation increment at the current hand origin, with no descent or terminal-edge translation. Its entire finger, hand and arm swept volume must first be supported as collision-free by legal observations and robot geometry. The supplied measurements do not establish that condition; if it cannot be established, hold position. Fixed hand-origin height alone does not guarantee finger clearance.

observed_evidence: The selected connected surface is approximately horizontal: fitted normal is nearly +z, plane center z is 0.063286 m, and plane RMS is 0.000151 m.
Pixel [300,174] measures world position [0.565748,0.066927,0.063654] m on that visible surface.
The terminal strip has observed x bounds 0.563001–0.584847 m and y span 0.115465 m. The y span exceeds the nominal 0.080 m maximum jaw opening.
Neither the supplied depth samples nor the images establish underside support, board/cooler separation, or a clear lower-jaw route.
The historical interior image provides qualitative motherboard/case context only, contingent on the stated static-object assumption.
inferred_geometry: A local sideways pinch near the terminal end avoids needing to straddle the 115 mm planar width.

For a PCB-only pinch, the lower jaw must reach beneath the PCB. Where the cooler overlaps this neighborhood, that requires entry into the board/cooler gap. An exposed overhang or a sufficiently large gap is an explicit unverified assumption.
A PCB-plus-cooler pinch would instead require a reachable cooler underside and total local thickness within the jaw opening. Neither is measured.
The measured terminal-strip x extent is not a grasp thickness or proof of two opposing edges.
risks: A lower jaw could strike the cooler, motherboard, components or case before reaching an opposing surface.
The proposed +x entry side is not certified free of case wall; no low external wall-side approach is proposed.

Avoidance requires keeping both fingers outside the case and motherboard envelopes throughout reorientation and insertion, not merely keeping the palm above the PCB. Those envelopes are insufficiently measured here.
PCB components, edge loading and unsupported board bending make even the visible upper-contact neighborhood uncertified.
Neither another 10 mm retreat nor repetition of the failed low external inspection is part of this proposal.
rejection_reason: Not rejected as a simulator-only hypothesis. Contact and insertion remain blocked specifically by the unobserved opposing surface, unknown lower-jaw access and unverified case/motherboard clearance. A top-down full-width y straddle is rejected because the observed span already exceeds maximum opening.
